attribution_limitations: Age is given in the case lead without a stated time point; the CVA was in 2018 and the pallidotomy in May 2022.
The text places major depressive disorder 18 months after CVA, while Table 1 gives May 2019 for the diagnosis and February 2018 for the CVA; the interval does not match.

Table 1 dates the one-month, three-month and six-month postsurgical follow-ups in 2023 and the one-year follow-up in May 2023, while the pallidotomy is dated May 2022; the dates do not fit the stated intervals or each other.

The text says movements began within a few weeks after CVA; Table 1 gives March 2018 for the start of the movement disorder. These are consistent in order but state different time forms; the table date was used on the fact.
Three times a day (TDS) follows diphenhydramine; it is unclear whether it also applies to haloperidol 0.5 mg.
Aripiprazole is written as 5 mg 1/2 BD without explaining the fraction.

The drug trials are listed without dates; Table 1 only gives a pharmacological treatment period of March 2018 to May 2022. The 2022 recurrence is stated for HC movements, and the second drug list follows it only in paragraph order.
The text says we did not see anyone after stating no adverse events or complications; the object of this sentence is unclear.

Follow-up is described as 12 months with examinations at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months, yet the author also states the patient could not be followed for more than one year; the discussion sentence on improved QOL has no quality-of-life measure.
Video 1 is cited for the movements and their control only as an external link to the journal website; the source declares no PMC media asset for it.

The text dates the brain MRI to 2018 and cites Figures 1 and 2, but the burned-in overlay on Figure 2 shows a scan date in a later year (identifier values not copied); the caption calls the images pre-operative.
